locator.text: Equation (9.19), p. 113, in the proof of Lemma 9.8

evidence: paper: \begin{array}{r|c} \text{radial physical derivative} & 1/2 + h\kappa_s \\ \text{axial physical derivative} & D = 1/2 - h \\ \text{time physical derivative} & 1 + h \\ \text{derivative of the cylindrical frame} & 1/2. \end{array} \tag{9.19}

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The table is not one declaration; its four rows are spread over several, and every row is covered. Time row (1+h): native_time_power_le states Tg^i ≤ Q^(-(1+h)), the paper's T_g^{i_0} = O(Q^{-1-h} S_*^P) without the S factor; the slow part of the time derivative is the -Q^(-1) entry of chartLinear. Axial row (D = 1/2 - h): CoordinateAlgebra.D is that number and chartLinear puts Q^(-D h) on the z coordinate; nativeGraph does not depend on z. Radial row (1/2 + hκ_s): norm_scaledRadial_le gives Q^(-1/2) and native_radial_power_le gives radialCoefficient ≤ Q^(-hκ) with kappa = 1/100000 (the paper's κ_s = 10^-5, p. 63 (6.2) and p. 100); radialCoefficient is the paper's M_i = Λ^i Q^{d_r/2} of (6.6). The two are multiplied in the proof of nativeGraph_positive_jet_bound (line 95-97) into Q^(-hκ - k/2), which at k = 1 is the printed exponent and for k > 1 is slightly better than k(1/2 + hκ_s). Frame row (1/2): no declaration states a Q-power cost for the frame. It follows from stated ones: rotation x is rotationMap (liftXY x) by definition, liftXY (physicalLift h n p) = scaledRadial n p (liftXY_physicalLift), so the frame along the physical lift is rotationMap ∘ scaledRadial n, and norm_jet_comp_linear with norm_scaledRadial_le charges Q^(-1/2) per derivative against jets of rotationMap that are bounded on the annulus (the compactness bound used inside rotationMap_jets). I did not find this composite written out anywhere. Downstream the repository does not keep the rows apart: physicalLift_positive_jet_bound charges the worst row Q^(-k(1+h)) for every direction, and SharpPhysicalCarrier.derivativeCost = 1 + 3h/2 is the single cost carried forward. The paper uses (9.19) the same way, only as something its costs s_x, s_t dominate.
